company.text: Novogene was founded in Beijing in 2011 by Dr. Ruiqiang Li and listed on the Shanghai STAR Market on April 13, 2021. It runs local labs in the US, UK and Singapore plus subsidiaries in Hong Kong, the Netherlands, Japan and elsewhere, and works with researchers in 70 countries and regions. Its US sequencing center sits on the **UC Davis** campus (announced April 2016). Services cover whole-genome, exome and transcriptome sequencing, single-cell and spatial omics, epigenomics, proteomics and metabolomics, with bioinformatics. Its rare and complex disease offer covers variant discovery, transcriptome and pathway analysis and multi-omics integration, for research use only.

industry.title: RNA joins DNA in rare disease
industry.text: Diagnostic yield from DNA-only testing stays below half of rare-disease cases (PhiTech cites under 40%); adding transcriptomics is the main route to close the gap — the reason G&M exists.

industry.title: Service labs move up the value chain
industry.text: Sequencing is a price-driven business; Novogene's 2025 profit fell 15% on 4.7% revenue growth. Interpretation and multi-omics analysis are where providers look for margin.

industry.title: BIOSECURE Act
industry.text: The revised BIOSECURE Act became US law on Dec 18, 2025 (FY26 NDAA). OMB must publish its list of biotechnology companies of concern by December 2026. The enacted law names no companies, and **Novogene is not named** in the analyses reviewed — but Chinese-owned sequencing providers will be watching the list.
